system: Movement collision push-out (resolveObstacles)
what: Pushes a circle of radius r out of every crate and wall box (barracks walls included, since they are addBox obstacles), using oriented boxes when rotated. It does the same for house colliders (oriented via their local boxes), cover boxes (skipped when standing above the top), tree squares and solid prop boxes, by the shortest axis. It is almost allocation-free: an unrotated legacy house that has no compound boxes allocates a one-element array per call (`h.boxes||[h.box]`), and Cabana has two (brickFarm at rot 0). The player, bots, the nav grid and the editor playtest all share it.

v2_note: Keep one collision function shared by players, bots and navigation, so bots and humans can never disagree. Avoid: a single sequential pass by shortest axis can jitter or leak in corners where boxes overlap. It scans every collider for every agent with no spatial index, which is O(agents × colliders) at 48+ players. Buildings, platforms and ramps rely on tickVertical's step guard rather than push-out; barracks walls are ordinary obstacles and do use push-out. Rust version: a broad-phase grid, oriented boxes and circles, and a deterministic fixed tick. Keep the ≥ 6 m gap rule (LOOP_V2 §9).
reason: Movement collision is decided by the authoritative sim.

system: Vertical surface query, step-up guard, gravity and jump
what: surfaceHeightAt returns the highest walkable top under a point: platforms, ramp slopes, live buildings and, optionally, cover tops. tickVertical blocks moving onto anything more than a step above the feet (sliding per axis), then applies jump, gravity and landing. It is zero-allocation and shared by the player and bots.

system: Team structures, enterable barracks, the map resupply terminal and the map spawn
what: makeBuilding builds a destructible team building as a box body with an accent trim band, a type label and a world health bar: HQ, refinery, power plant, or a plain 'barracks' box (the K glyph in the Cabana grid). It registers it in the buildings array with health from T, a world box and an editor tag. makeBarracks builds the enterable barracks: five addBox walls with a door gap (so they are ordinary obstacles), a lintel, a floor, a roof with its own cloned transparent material so it can fade, a BARRACKS label, and an ARMORY panel on the back wall whose panelPos is where the player opens the shop (nearPanel: within 2.6 m of an own-team barracks panel only, sameTeam check at :2793; elsewhere E falls back to the map terminal within 6 m, :2795).
